title: Activists Raise Alarm Over Military-Grade Steel Shipments From India to Israel
summary: Activists have flagged six shipments of suspected military-grade steel traveling from India to Israel aboard a Swiss vessel, intensifying scrutiny of military supply chains during the ongoing Middle East conflict.
contents:
## India-Israel Military Supply Controversy

### Shipment Details
Activists have raised alarm over what they describe as a "flood" of military supplies flowing from India to Israel. Six shipments of suspected military-grade steel have departed India aboard a Swiss-registered commercial vessel bound for Israeli ports. The shipments arrived amid heightened global scrutiny of arms transfers to Israel during its ongoing military operations.

### UAE-Israel Defense Cooperation
Separately, the United Arab Emirates and Israel have launched a joint fund dedicated to defense acquisitions, according to former and current U.S. officials. The fund represents a deepening of the Abraham Accords-era security relationship between the two nations, despite growing regional tensions stemming from the Iran-U.S. conflict that erupted on February 28.

### Broader Context
The military supply revelations come at a sensitive moment in the Middle East conflict. Israeli strikes have killed more than 3,000 people in Lebanon since early March, according to Lebanon's health ministry, with another 9,273 wounded. Five people died in Israeli strikes on Gaza near a community kitchen in Deir Al-Balah.

### International Reactions
The Far-right Unite the Kingdom rally organized by British activist Tommy Robinson in London on Saturday featured Islamophobic speeches that sparked widespread condemnation on social media, reflecting growing polarization over Middle East policy in Western democracies.

title: U.S. Treasury Extends 30-Day Sanctions Waiver on Russian At-Sea Oil as Brent Crude Surges Past $111
summary: The U.S. Treasury extended its sanctions waiver for Russian oil cargoes already at sea by 30 days while Brent crude surged past $111 per barrel amid stalled Iran peace talks and drone attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure.
contents:
## Oil Markets and Sanctions Update

### Russian Oil Sanctions Waiver
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Monday a temporary 30-day general license extending the sanctions waiver for Russian oil cargoes already at sea. The extension aims to provide energy-vulnerable nations with continued access to Russian crude currently stranded in transit. Bessent stated the license would help stabilize the physical crude market while reducing China's ability to stockpile discounted oil.

### Oil Price Surge
Brent crude futures climbed $2.03 to $111.29 per barrel, touching $112 overnight — the highest level since May 5. West Texas Intermediate crude reached $108.70 before settling at $107.73, up 2.19 percent. Both benchmark contracts gained more than seven percent last week as prospects for a peace deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz continued to fade.

### Strait of Hormuz Traffic
Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz recovered slightly last week, with 55 commodity vessels crossing between May 11 and 17, according to maritime tracking firm Kpler. The previous week recorded just 19 crossings — the lowest weekly figure since the first U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. Iranian state television reported the Revolutionary Guards permitted more ships to transit the strait.

### Shadow Fleet Activity
Russian crude oil exports hit 3.7 million barrels per day in April, the highest since December 2025. Sanctioned shadow tankers carried a record 54 percent of Russia's fossil fuel exports. Iran has not successfully exported any crude oil by sea for 28 days amid the U.S. naval blockade, according to TankerTrackers monitoring data.

title: Kim Jong Un Orders Military to Transform Southern Border Into Impregnable Fortress
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un convened an unprecedented meeting of division and brigade commanders, ordering the strengthening of front-line units along the southern border and instructing commanders to raise vigilance against South Korea, described as the arch enemy.
contents:
## North Korean Military Buildup Orders

### Commander Meeting
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un convened a meeting on May 17 with commanding officers of divisions and brigades across the entire military — the first such gathering since he took power. An estimated 180 to 250 operational commanders from the army, navy, air forces, and strategic missile units attended the session at the Party Central Committee headquarters in Pyongyang.

### Defense Directives
Kim set forth plans to strengthen first-line units and other major military formations as "an important decision to more thoroughly deter war." He directed commanders to redefine operational concepts in line with rapid military modernization and adjust training systems to reflect changes in modern warfare. Analysts noted these instructions appeared informed by developments in Russia's war with Ukraine, where North Korean troops have gained combat experience.

### Border Fortification
Kim emphasized the ruling party's "policy of territorial defence on strengthening the first-line units in the southern border and turning the border line into an impregnable fortress." This reinforced the current deployment plan for 250 new tactical ballistic missile launchers and three battalions of 155mm self-propelled artillery in the front area.

### Inter-Korean Context
The orders came the same day South Korea's Unification Ministry released its 2026 white paper shifting focus toward peaceful coexistence between "two states" rather than reunification. References to "peace" surged from 108 to 627 compared to last year's edition, while mentions of "North Korean human rights" dropped from 288 to 47.

title: Iran Responds to U.S. Peace Proposal as IRGC Threatens Permits for Hormuz Internet Cables
summary: Iran conveyed a revised counter-proposal to the United States through Pakistani mediators while the IRGC announced that fiber-optic internet cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz could face a new permit system, escalating Tehran's control over the critical waterway.
contents:
## Iran Peace Negotiations and Hormuz Escalation

### Revised Peace Proposal
Iran's foreign ministry announced Monday that Tehran had responded to the latest U.S. proposal aimed at ending the 80-day war. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei confirmed exchanges continued through Pakistani mediation without providing specific details. The U.S. had presented a five-point list demanding Iran keep only one nuclear site operational and transfer its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to American custody.

### IRGC Internet Cable Threat
Iran's Revolutionary Guard announced Monday that internet fiber-optic cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz could fall under a new permit regime. The Guard cited Iran's "absolute sovereignty over the bed and subsoil of its territorial sea" as justification for potentially requiring permits for all submarine cables transiting the waterway. This represented a significant escalation in Tehran's efforts to assert comprehensive control over the strategic strait.

### Nuclear Negotiations Impasse
Iran declared its nuclear enrichment rights "remain non-negotiable," with spokesman Baqaei stating enrichment constitutes an existing right rather than a concession. Tehran rejected the U.S. demand to transfer enriched uranium, insisting on full sanctions relief and war reparations as preconditions for any agreement.

### Military Escalation Risks
U.S. officials confirmed President Trump convened top national security advisers over the weekend, with the Pentagon preparing military target plans including strikes on Iranian energy and infrastructure sites. The New York Times reported the U.S. and Israel engaged in the "most extensive operational planning" since last month's ceasefire, with operations potentially resuming within days.

title: Vietnam Hands Over Rescued Chinese Fishermen and Vessels in Gulf of Tonkin Maritime Cooperation
summary: Vietnamese authorities completed the handover of two fishing vessels and 10 Chinese fishermen rescued in the Gulf of Tonkin, demonstrating bilateral maritime cooperation despite ongoing South China Sea territorial disputes.
contents:
## Vietnam-China Maritime Rescue Cooperation

### Rescue Operation
Vietnamese authorities on May 11 completed the handover of two fishing vessels and 10 Chinese fishermen rescued in the Gulf of Tonkin to Chinese law enforcement forces. The transfer took place in waters along the Gulf of Tonkin delimitation line, approximately 20 nautical miles east of Bach Long Vi Island.

### Humanitarian Assistance
The Hai Phong Border Guard Command coordinated the handover in cooperation with Border Guard Flotilla 38 and Coast Guard Region 1 Command. All 10 fishermen maintained stable physical and mental conditions after receiving humanitarian support on Bach Long Vi Island. Vietnamese authorities provided photographs and video footage of the rescue operation and vessel repairs to ensure transparency.

### Bilateral Cooperation
A representative of the Hainan Sub-bureau under the China Coast Guard expressed appreciation for the timely assistance provided by Vietnamese forces. The rescued fishermen sent letters of thanks to Vietnamese forces for conducting the rescue despite difficult conditions and providing thoughtful humanitarian care.

### Regional Security Framework
Following the handover, both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation in safeguarding maritime sovereignty, combating illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing, maintaining effective communication channels, and enhancing disaster response capabilities. The cooperation occurred against the backdrop of persistent territorial disputes in the South China Sea, where multiple nations including Vietnam and China maintain competing sovereignty claims.

title: Chinese Military Conducts Joint Drills in East China Sea Following Japanese MSDF Taiwan Strait Transit
summary: China's military held joint exercises in the East China Sea, responding to a recent transit of the Taiwan Strait by Japan's Maritime Self-Defense Force, amid growing tensions over regional military activities and U.S. security commitments.
contents:
## Chinese Military Exercises in East China Sea

### Exercise Details
The Chinese military conducted joint drills in the East China Sea following a transit of the Taiwan Strait by Japan's Maritime Self-Defense Force (MSDF). The exercises demonstrated China's capability to project military power in contested waters and signaled Beijing's opposition to what it views as provocative naval transits near Taiwan.

### Regional Military Dynamics
Trump recently indicated willingness to discuss U.S. arms sales to Taiwan with Chinese President Xi Jinping, raising anxiety in the region about shifting U.S. security commitments. The discussion came during Trump's high-stakes visit to Beijing, where the Iran war and trade dominated the agenda while Taiwan received less prominent attention.

### CSIS Analysis Context
The CSIS China Power Project has tracked a sustained increase in Chinese military activities across the Indo-Pacific region. Beijing maintains extensive naval, coast guard, and maritime militia presence in the South China Sea, East China Sea, and Taiwan Strait, deploying forces to challenge competing territorial claims.

### Japan Defense Posture
Japan recently sealed its largest-ever defense contract with a frigate sale to Australia, reflecting Tokyo's growing military engagement across the Indo-Pacific. Japan pledged "all possible measures" for Hormuz safety while strengthening security cooperation with the United States and regional partners amid escalating geopolitical tensions.

title: Philippines Deploys Aircraft to Challenge Chinese Research Vessel Conducting Unauthorized Surveys in West Philippine Sea
summary: The Philippine Coast Guard deployed aircraft to issue radio warnings to the Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 operating near the oil-rich Reed Bank, while monitoring 41 Chinese maritime militia vessels swarming nearby reefs.
contents:
## Philippine Maritime Sovereignty Challenge

### Research Vessel Detection
The Philippine Coast Guard detected Chinese research vessel Xiang Yang Hong 33 conducting unauthorized marine scientific research near Iroquois Reef at the southern end of Reed Bank, an area thought to contain significant natural gas and oil deposits. The vessel deployed a service boat toward the reef, confirming ongoing unauthorized research operations within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone.

### Maritime Militia Presence
During the same patrol, Philippine forces monitored one Chinese Coast Guard vessel and 13 Chinese maritime militia ships around Iroquois Reef, plus 28 additional militia vessels anchored near Philippine-occupied Thitu Island. The Armed Forces of the Philippines reported tracking 35 Chinese naval and coast guard vessels across four key features in the West Philippine Sea between May 4 and 11.

### Sovereignty Assertion
PCG Commandant Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan declared the Chinese activities a "clear and blatant violation" of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The Philippines utilized Canada's Dark Vessel Detection System to track the research vessel, which had conducted survey activities across multiple features since departing China on April 15.

### Regional Tensions
The confrontation extended ongoing friction between Manila and Beijing, which claims nearly the entire South China Sea despite a 2016 international ruling that its assertion has "no legal basis." Earlier this month, Philippine civilians planted a Philippine flag on Sandy Cay, a disputed sandbar near Thitu Island, prompting a strong Chinese response.

title: U.S. CENTCOM Reports 85 Vessels Redirected Under Iranian Port Blockade as Oil Tanker Traffic Remains Constrained
summary: U.S. Central Command reported redirecting 85 commercial vessels and disabling four others under the ongoing blockade of Iranian ports, while at least 37 oil-laden Iranian tankers remained trapped within the Persian Gulf.
contents:
## Iranian Port Blockade Maritime Intelligence

### Blockade Enforcement
U.S. Central Command announced Monday that American naval forces have redirected 85 commercial vessels and disabled four others since the blockade of Iranian ports commenced on April 13. CENTCOM stated it continues to "strictly enforce the U.S. blockade against Iranian ports," focusing primarily on large VLCC tankers rather than smaller carriers.

### Iranian Oil Fleet Status
The United Against Nuclear Iran monitoring group identified at least 37 tankers laden with Iranian oil — primarily crude — currently operating inside the Persian Gulf west of the Strait of Hormuz. At Chabahar Port outside the Persian Gulf, 13 Iran-flagged tankers loaded with Iranian oil anchored while awaiting opportunities to cross the blockade perimeter.

### Kharg Island Disruption
Iran's Kharg Island — the hub handling 90 percent of Iranian oil exports — has not loaded any tankers since May 6, following a suspected oil spill that satellite imagery showed spreading across approximately 45 square kilometers of water. TankerTrackers confirmed Iran has not successfully exported any crude oil by sea for 28 days.

### Shadow Fleet Evasion Tactics
Iranian tankers have adopted new evasion routes through the Indian Ocean and Indonesia's Lombok Strait to avoid interdiction in the Malacca and Singapore Straits. Multiple Iran-flagged vessels conducted ship-to-ship transfers at the Eastern Outer Port Limits anchorage off Johor, Malaysia, maintaining covert supply chains to Chinese refineries despite the blockade.

title: South Korea Releases Unification White Paper Shifting Focus to Peaceful Coexistence as North Korean Football Team Arrives
summary: South Korea's Unification Ministry released its 2026 white paper reframing inter-Korean relations around peaceful coexistence between two states, while a North Korean women's football team arrived in the South for the first such visit in nearly eight years.
contents:
## South Korean Policy Shift on North Korea

### White Paper Release
The South Korean Unification Ministry released its 2026 white paper on Monday, articulating three core principles guiding the Lee Jae Myung administration's North Korea policy: respecting the North's political system, not pursuing absorption of North Korea, and refraining from hostile acts. The document marked a significant departure from the previous Yoon Suk Yeol administration's hard-line approach.

### Language Analysis
References to "peace" or "peaceful coexistence" surged from 108 in last year's edition to 627. Mentions of "dialogue" rose from 50 to 144. Conversely, references to "North Korean human rights" dropped sharply from 288 to 47, with the topic downgraded from a standalone chapter to a brief subsection. Mentions of "freedom" fell from 118 to 16.

### North Korean Football Visit
A North Korean women's football team arrived in South Korea on Sunday — the first visit by a North Korean sports team in nearly eight years — to compete in the Asian Champions League semifinals. The historic visit raised cautious optimism about a potential thaw in inter-Korean relations, though Pyongyang remained unresponsive to Seoul's repeated offers for unconditional dialogue.

### Constitutional Context
The policy shift came as North Korea's recently revised constitution dropped all references to Korean unification and redefined its territory to exclude the southern half of the Korean Peninsula. Unification Minister Chung Dong-young stated the government aimed to "practice peace through actions, not words" and encouraged the two Koreas to "sit face to face again as neighbors."

title: Russia Launches 524 Drones and 22 Missiles Across Eight Ukrainian Regions Wounding Dozens
summary: Russia targeted eight regions of Ukraine in a massive nighttime drone and missile barrage, firing 524 attack drones and 22 ballistic and cruise missiles that wounded more than two dozen civilians including three children, with Dnipro bearing the heaviest damage over a six-hour assault.
contents:
## Massive Overnight Barrage

Russian forces fired 524 attack drones and 22 ballistic and cruise missiles across eight Ukrainian regions beginning early on the evening of May 17 and continuing overnight, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported Monday. The barrage represented one of the largest single aerial attacks in recent months, following an escalating spiral of long-range strikes after a May 9-11 ceasefire produced little impact.

## Dnipro Bears Heaviest Damage

The Dnipropetrovsk region endured a six-hour bombardment that struck energy facilities and residential buildings. At least 26 people, including two children, sustained injuries in the region, according to Ukraine's emergency service. Regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha confirmed that apartment blocks, a religious institution, and a university suffered damage.

## Odesa and Other Regions Targeted

Russian drones also damaged residential buildings, a school, and a kindergarten in the major Black Sea export port of Odesa, injuring an 11-year-old boy and a 59-year-old man. Ukrainian energy firm Naftogaz reported that drones struck several of its facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region overnight. Damage also affected Ukraine's Chernihiv and Zaporizhzhia regions.

## Escalation After Failed Ceasefire

The barrage continued a recent spiral of long-range strikes that have grown in scale since a brief ceasefire attempt earlier in May. Ukraine responded with its own large-scale drone attack on Russia over the weekend, killing at least four people including three near Moscow. Zelenskyy claimed Ukraine's expanding long-range capabilities have significantly changed the situation and global perceptions of the conflict.

title: Iran Threatens Permit Requirements for Internet Fiber Optic Cables Passing Through Strait of Hormuz
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard announced that internet fiber optic cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz could face a new permit system, citing absolute sovereignty over its territorial seabed as Tehran expands control measures beyond shipping to undersea communications infrastructure.
contents:
## IRGC Announces Cable Permit Threat

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps declared Monday that internet fiber optic cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz could face a new permit and regulatory system. The IRGC stated that following the imposition of control over the strait, Iran could declare all fiber-optic cables passing through the waterway subject to permits, citing absolute sovereignty over the bed and subsoil of its territorial sea.

## Critical Infrastructure Vulnerability

The Strait of Hormuz serves not only as a vital oil and gas shipping corridor but also as a pathway for multiple submarine fiber optic cables connecting Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. These cables carry a significant portion of global internet traffic, making any disruption a potential threat to international communications, financial markets, and data flows across multiple continents.

## Geospatial and Mapping Implications

The cable infrastructure traversing the strait represents a critical node in global telecommunications networks. Geospatial analysis of the strait's seabed reveals concentrated cable routes running through narrow channels, creating a single point of failure for intercontinental data connectivity. Any enforcement action against these cables would affect satellite-dependent geospatial intelligence operations, maritime tracking systems, and real-time mapping services throughout the region.

## Expanding Iranian Control Measures

The cable permit threat follows Iran's establishment of the Persian Gulf Strait Authority to manage and toll commercial shipping through the waterway. Tehran has progressively expanded its control claims from surface vessel traffic to subsurface infrastructure, signaling a comprehensive strategy to leverage Hormuz as an instrument of geopolitical pressure beyond traditional maritime domain.

title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts Three Drones Entering Airspace from Iraq Amid Regional Escalation
summary: Saudi Arabia announced the interception of three drones that entered its airspace from Iraq, warning of necessary operational measures against sovereignty violations, as regional tensions persist despite the ceasefire between the US and Iran.
contents:
## Saudi Air Defense Intercepts Iraqi-Origin Drones

Saudi Arabian authorities announced Monday the interception of three unmanned aerial vehicles that entered the kingdom's airspace from Iraqi territory. The Saudi defense establishment warned it would take all necessary operational measures to respond to any attempt to violate its sovereignty and security.

## Pattern of Post-Ceasefire Drone Attacks

Despite a ceasefire that came into effect in April following the US-Israel conflict with Iran, drones have continued launching from Iraq toward Gulf countries including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. Iraqi-based Iranian proxy militias possess advanced drone capabilities and have repeatedly targeted Gulf state infrastructure throughout the conflict.

## Connection to UAE Nuclear Plant Strike

The Saudi drone interception occurred on the same day the United Arab Emirates condemned a drone strike that targeted the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in the Al Dhafra region of Abu Dhabi. The UAE Defense Ministry reported that three drones entered from its western border, with two intercepted and one striking an electrical generator outside the plant's inner perimeter. Saudi Arabia expressed solidarity with the UAE, calling the nuclear plant attack a threat to regional stability.

## Broader Security Implications

Iranian military cooperation with African nations and proxy groups across the Middle East continues to reshape regional security dynamics. The drone attacks highlight the persistent vulnerability of Gulf state critical infrastructure to asymmetric threats, even during periods of nominal ceasefire between major belligerents.

title: SpaceX Dragon CRS-34 Docks at International Space Station Delivering 6,500 Pounds of Science and Supplies
summary: The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft successfully docked at the International Space Station's Harmony module on May 17, delivering nearly 6,500 pounds of cargo including the STORIE space weather instrument, CLARREO Pathfinder calibration tool, and bone research experiments for the Expedition 74 crew.
contents:
## Dragon Arrives at Orbital Outpost

The SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft docked to the forward port of the International Space Station's Harmony module at 6:37 a.m. EDT on Saturday, completing the 34th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission for NASA. The uncrewed Dragon carried nearly 6,500 pounds of food, supplies, and scientific equipment for the seven-member Expedition 74 crew.

## New Science Experiments Delivered

Among the scientific payloads, the STORIE (Storm Time O+ Ring current Imaging Evolution) instrument will monitor charged particles orbiting Earth that respond to space weather and can affect power grids and satellites. The CLARREO Pathfinder instrument will take highly accurate measurements of sunlight reflected by Earth and the Moon, providing calibration data five to ten times more accurate than existing sensors.

## Additional Research Hardware

The Dragon also delivered the ODYSSEY experiment to evaluate how well Earth-based microgravity simulators recreate space conditions, the Green Bone investigation studying bone cells growing on wood-derived scaffolds in microgravity, and the SPARK evaluation of red blood cell and spleen changes during spaceflight. The Laplace experiment will study dust particle collisions to advance understanding of planetary formation.

## Mission Milestones

The mission launched on May 15 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. This flight marked the sixth mission for this particular Dragon capsule, setting a new record for SpaceX cargo spacecraft reuse. NASA astronauts Jack Hathaway and ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot monitored the automated docking approach.

title: US Treasury Extends 30-Day Sanctions Waiver for Russian Oil Tankers Stranded at Sea
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a temporary 30-day general license extending the sanctions waiver for Russian oil cargoes already at sea, providing vulnerable nations continued access to stranded Russian oil while reducing China's ability to stockpile discounted crude.
contents:
## Sanctions Waiver Extension Announced

The US Treasury on Monday extended its sanctions waiver for Russian oil cargoes currently at sea by 30 days through a new temporary general license. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the extension via X, stating the waiver would provide the most vulnerable nations with the ability to temporarily access Russian oil currently stranded at sea.

## Strategic Objectives of the License

Bessent emphasized that the general license serves multiple strategic purposes beyond humanitarian energy access. The extension aims to help stabilize the physical crude market, ensure oil reaches the most energy-vulnerable countries, and help reroute existing supply to countries most in need by reducing China's ability to stockpile discounted oil.

## Fleet and Vessel Implications

The waiver directly affects dozens of tankers carrying Russian crude that have remained anchored or in transit across global shipping lanes since the escalation of sanctions enforcement. These vessels — many operating as part of the documented shadow fleet carrying Russian petroleum — have faced increasing restrictions as Western nations tighten enforcement against sanctions evasion networks.

## Market Response and Energy Security

The announcement came as Brent crude oil prices fluctuated around $108-112 per barrel on Monday, with markets responding to competing signals from the Iran conflict and global energy supply concerns. The 30-year US Treasury bond yield climbed to 5.16 percent, its highest since October 2023, as inflation fears driven by elevated energy costs continued to rattle global bond markets.

title: US Aircraft Respond to PLA Pilot Demands in Taiwan's ADIZ as China Tracks Seven Military Planes Around Island
summary: Military watchers intercepted radio communications showing Chinese PLA Navy Air Force pilots issuing demands to Taiwanese aircraft in the southwestern ADIZ, while nearby US military aircraft broadcast responses asserting lawful rights to operate in international airspace.
contents:
## Radio Intercepts Reveal PLA-US Confrontation

Military watchers intercepted pilot radio communications on Monday revealing Chinese People's Liberation Army Navy Air Force pilots issuing consecutive demands to Taiwanese aircraft at 8:57 a.m., 8:59 a.m., and 9:00 a.m. local time. The PLA pilots claimed Taiwanese aircraft endangered flight safety and demanded they maintain a safe distance within Taiwan's southwestern air defense identification zone.

## US Military Aircraft Assert International Rights

Nearby US military aircraft broadcast messages as many as nine times in response to the Chinese demands, asserting their lawful right to operate in international airspace. One US military aircraft reiterated that its operations had taken into consideration the rights of all countries, directly rejecting the Chinese military demands.

## Taiwan Defense Ministry Tracking Report

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense tracked seven Chinese military aircraft, five naval vessels, and one official ship operating around Taiwan between 6 a.m. Sunday and 6 a.m. Monday. All seven PLA aircraft crossed the Taiwan Strait median line, entering Taiwan's northern and southwestern ADIZ. Taiwan deployed aircraft, naval ships, and coastal-based missile systems to monitor the activity.

## Monthly Escalation Pattern

So far in May 2026, the ministry has tracked Chinese military aircraft 120 times and ships 132 times, continuing the sustained gray-zone pressure campaign that Beijing has maintained since September 2020. The intercepts occurred days after the Trump-Xi Beijing summit, where cross-strait relations featured prominently in discussions.

title: Former AIT Director Warns China Shifting from Peaceful Development to Aggressive Urgent Approach Toward Taiwan
summary: Former American Institute in Taiwan director William Stanton warned at a Taipei seminar that China has moved from seeking peaceful development to a more aggressive and urgent stance toward Taiwan, employing heightened military intimidation and gray-zone tactics following the Trump-Xi Beijing summit.
contents:
## Ex-AIT Head Analyzes China's Strategic Shift

Former American Institute in Taiwan director William Stanton addressed a Taipei seminar hosted by the World United Formosans for Independence on Sunday, warning that China's approach to Taiwan has fundamentally shifted. Stanton characterized the transition as moving from a peaceful development framework to a more aggressive and urgent stance.

## Gray-Zone Warfare and Military Intimidation

Stanton detailed Beijing's employment of heightened military intimidation through gray-zone tactics, deploying ships and aircraft near Taiwan's territorial waters and airspace with increasing frequency. China has also intensified political warfare campaigns to isolate Taiwan, emphasizing its one country two systems formula as the only viable model for cross-strait relations.

## Trump's Transactional Approach

Stanton noted that while Trump initially treated Taiwan as a key strategic partner and a card to use against China — approving more arms sales and lifting restrictions on high-level official meetings — his second term has brought a much more transactional approach. Trump now links defense commitments to semiconductors and economics, creating uncertainty about the depth of US support.

## Targeting Independence Advocates

Beijing has specifically targeted Taiwanese independence advocates, including officials deemed hardliners, implementing a two-pronged strategy combining the threat of force with economic incentives and united front activities. Stanton emphasized that the idea of forced unification serves as a measure of Xi Jinping's political ambitions and the broader Chinese Communist Party agenda for national rejuvenation.

title: US Central Command Reports 85 Commercial Vessels Redirected in Ongoing Iran Naval Blockade
summary: CENTCOM announced Monday that US military forces have now redirected 85 commercial vessels and disabled four others as part of the ongoing naval blockade against Iranian ports, while Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened to turn the Gulf of Oman into a graveyard for ships if the US does not end the blockade.
contents:
## Blockade Enforcement Escalation

US Central Command announced midday Monday that the military has redirected 85 commercial vessels amid the ongoing naval blockade of Iranian ports, up from 84 vessels reported just hours earlier. CENTCOM confirmed that US forces have also disabled four vessels attempting to breach the blockade since it began on April 13, 2026.

## Iran Threatens Gulf of Oman Retaliation

In response to the continued blockade enforcement, Iran's top military adviser warned that Tehran would turn the Gulf of Oman into a graveyard for ships if the United States does not cease its naval operations. The Revolutionary Guard Corps has maintained that the Strait of Hormuz falls under Iranian sovereignty and that approaching vessels without authorization would face targeting.

## Maritime Traffic Disruption

Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic showed a modest recovery last week, with 55 commodities vessels crossing the strategic waterway between May 11 and 17, according to maritime tracking firm Kpler. The previous week had recorded only 19 crossings, the lowest weekly figure since the first US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. Despite the increase, traffic remains far below peacetime levels.

## Regional Naval Security Impact

The dual blockade dynamic — with the US restricting Iranian port access and Iran controlling Hormuz transit — has created unprecedented maritime security challenges in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman. Philippine and other regional coast guard operations have monitored the situation as disrupted shipping routes affect fuel prices and supply chains across the Indo-Pacific.

title: Over Half of South Sudan Population Faces Acute Hunger Crisis with Famine Risk
summary: UN agencies warned that 7.8 million people in South Sudan, representing 56 percent of the population, face high levels of acute food insecurity between April and July 2026, with a credible risk of famine in four counties amid escalating conflict and mass displacement.
contents:
## South Sudan Humanitarian Emergency

### Food Insecurity Scale
The Food and Agriculture Organization, World Food Programme, and UNICEF issued a joint warning that a deepening hunger crisis pushes 7.8 million people into high levels of acute food insecurity in South Sudan between April and July 2026. Among those projected to face acute food insecurity, 73,300 people confront catastrophic levels, the most severe classification under the IPC framework, representing a dramatic 160 percent increase from the previous estimate. An additional 2.5 million people face emergency-level conditions while 5.3 million face crisis-level food insecurity.

### Conflict-Driven Displacement
Violence in Jonglei State has displaced over 304,000 people since December 2025, with fighting between the South Sudan People Defence Forces and the Sudan People Liberation Army in Opposition destroying communities and cutting off humanitarian access. At least 33 health facilities have sustained damage or looting due to ongoing fighting, leaving an estimated 1.4 million people without access to health care.

### Famine Warning
UN agencies warned of a credible risk of famine in four counties across Upper Nile and Jonglei states under a worst-case scenario of escalating conflict, further displacement, and constrained humanitarian access. The IPC projected 11 counties to face extremely critical acute malnutrition outcomes, with 700,000 children projected to face severe acute malnutrition through July.

### Humanitarian Response Challenges
WFP Director of Emergencies Ross Smith described a critical race against time to expedite and increase deliveries to remote locations in anticipation of an early rainy season. Humanitarian access remains severely constrained by insecurity, coercion, interference, illegal taxation, and violence against personnel and assets across multiple states.
